flagged_cases.title: Clonogenic survival and relative biological effectiveness of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma under pristine and spread-out Bragg peak irradiation with protons and carbon ions.
flagged_cases.caption: Figure 6. RBE₁₀ as a function of LETD,1H or 12C for PANC-1 and BxPC-3 cells. Relative biological effectiveness at 10% surviving fraction (RBE₁₀) plotted against Monte Carlo–derived dose-averaged LET for ions of the same type as the primary beam (1H or 12C ions). Blue symbols represent 180.1 MeV proton sampling positions (entrance, proximal, peak, distal), and red symbols represent 352.4 MeV/u carbon ion sampling positions (entrance, proximal, pre-peak, peak). Purple and pink squares represent SOBP proton and carbon results, respectively. Error bars reflect propagated uncertainty from the fitted LQ parameter estimates used in the RBE calculation. Across the sampled pristine beam positions, RBE₁₀ increases with LETD for both ion species, with a steeper relationship observed for carbon ions at higher LET values. Alt text: Scatter plots show RBE₁₀ versus dose-averaged LETD for PANC-1 and BxPC-3 cells. RBE₁₀ increases gradually across pristine proton positions and more steeply across pristine carbon ion positions, with higher values in PANC-1 at the highest carbon ion LETD. Proton and carbon ion SOBP measurements are shown alongside the pristine-beam data.

flagged_cases.title: A Normative Model Reveals Functional Optimization of Synaptic Nano-Architecture
flagged_cases.caption: Figure 4: Glutamate release from the AZ center optimizes postsynaptic current ampli- tude. A-C: Statistical model of the synapse. GluRs (black dots) are randomly located around a ring (red circle) whose radius (121nm) corresponds to the average observed distance between GluRs and the center of AZ. We studied the effect of a simulated fusion event at a distance d from the center of the AZ. D: At each point of the AZ, the color code (blue scale) corresponds to the mean postsynaptic current µe following glutamate release at this location. µe is maximized for a release close to the center. E: Example synapse. The positions of GluRs (blue) was held fixed to their observed values. The optimal position for a release site to optimize h (red) was compared to actual Unc13A positions (green). F: The average distance between actual and µe-optimal release sites was compared to the distance between actual release sites and the center of the AZ (Ctrl. 1), a random GluR cluster position (Ctrl. 2), and a random position on the AZ disk (Ctrl. 3). G: Same as D, but plotting the average activation time < tmax > as a function of the release location. It is minimized for a release close to the center. H: µe as a function of the distance d between the release site and the AZ center (dark line) vs. observed Unc13A density (blue line). Yellow line: average observed distance to center for Unc13As (shaded area: s.d.). I: Observed density of nearest neighbor distances between Unc13As across all observed AZs.
